findings.title: Span buffer keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets without migration
findings.body: This line starts writing `span-buf:s:*` keys with `ZADD`, and the Lua script now uses `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZPOPMIN` while `_load_segment_data` uses `ZSCAN`. The key namespace and TTLs are unchanged, so old workers and existing keys still contain Redis SETs created by `SADD`/`SSCAN`. During a rolling deploy, or for up to `redis_ttl` seconds of pre-existing keys, new workers will hit `WRONGTYPE` on SET keys and old workers will hit `WRONGTYPE` on ZSET keys. That aborts span ingestion and flushing and can drop spans. A versioned key prefix or a dual read/write migration is needed.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the datetime order_by used by audit logs
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`, but `organization_auditlogs.py` instantiates it with `order_by=-datetime`, so the value is a `datetime`. `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result. Its `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw cursor integer instead of converting it back to a datetime, so later pages would compare a datetime column with an integer. Any audit-log request with `optimized_pagination=true` and the required permission will 500 instead of paginating. The optimized paginator needs the datetime conversion used by `DateTimePaginator`, or the endpoint needs a compatible paginator.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset path slices a Django QuerySet with a negative index
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and a user-supplied cursor has `offset < 0`, this branch calls `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing or negative slice starts and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, so a crafted cursor such as `?cursor=...:-1:0` on the audit-log endpoint produces a 500. Even if negative slicing were allowed, `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` remains positive, so `[-N:positive]` would return an empty or wrong page rather than reverse pagination. The negative-offset feature does not work as documented.

findings.title: Eviction cap is hard-coded to 1000 and ignores max_segment_spans
findings.body: The Lua eviction always keeps at most 1000 spans, while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` defaults to 1001 and is still accepted as a constructor argument. The Python-side `max_segment_spans` check was removed from `_load_segment_data`, so that setting is now a no-op: configuring a lower limit will not bound segment size, and the default behavior silently drops one span from a 1001-span segment instead of honoring the configured threshold. The cap should be passed into the script or enforced consistently in Python.

findings.title: No test exercises the new >1000-span eviction path
findings.body: All span-buffer tests in this file build segments of at most five spans, so the new `zpopmin` eviction branch is never executed. The hard-coded cap, interaction with `max_segment_spans`, cleanup of redirects and TTLs for evicted spans, and root-span retention under eviction are unverified. Add a test with more than 1000 spans in one segment and assert the intended survivors and key cleanup.
